title: Cooling measures and air-conditioning in Singapore schools
asked: Mr Cai Yinzhou asked which schools are most exposed to the urban heat island effect, what progress has been made on cool paint and ventilation at older campuses, and whether new school building standards will require passive cooling. He also asked how many classrooms are air-conditioned versus non-air-conditioned, and whether studies exist on thermal comfort and academic performance.
response: MOE designs schools for heat resilience using passive cooling: new schools target Green Mark Platinum Super Low Energy certification, with north-south orientation, shading, large windows and ceiling fans. By 2027, all schools will get additional, more powerful classroom fans and cool paint on external facades. Schools facing pervasive heat build-up from site constraints are being identified, and targeted cooling or air-conditioning may be added where classrooms must be enclosed for dust or noise. MOE is working with agencies and researchers on how rising temperatures affect student learning.

key_points.point: New schools are designed to meet Green Mark Platinum Super Low Energy certification, which emphasises passive design.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: All new schools are designed to achieve Green Mark Platinum Super Low Energy certification

key_points.point: School buildings are oriented north-south for natural cross-ventilation, with shading and large window openings supported by ceiling fans.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: school buildings are oriented in a north-south direction for natural cross-ventilation

key_points.point: By 2027, all schools will receive additional, more powerful classroom fans and cool paint on external building facades.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: By 2027, all schools will be provided with additional and more powerful fans for classrooms as well as the coating of external building facades with cool paint.

key_points.point: MOE is working with schools to identify those with pervasive heat build-up caused by site constraints or surroundings that block wind flow.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: We have also been working with schools to identify those that may experience pervasive heat build-up due to specific site constraints

key_points.point: Air-conditioning can be considered for classrooms that must be enclosed for long periods because of persistent dust or extreme noise, such as nearby construction.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: Air-conditioning can also be considered for classrooms that need to be enclosed for extended periods due to persistent dust or extreme noise

key_points.point: MOE is exploring further heat adaptation and active cooling measures, including mixed mode air-conditioning.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: This includes exploring further heat adaptation and active cooling measures for classrooms, such as mixed mode air-conditioning.

key_points.point: A 2024 National University of Singapore study found cognitive performance declines above a certain temperature threshold.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: we did have a 2024 National University of Singapore study that identified that cognitive performance does decline above a certain temperature threshold

key_points.point: MOE will target cooling measures at schools where students experience more discomfort, whether temporary or permanent.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: We will continue to look across our schools and target the measures at the ones where students may be experiencing more discomfort
